title: Marathon
note: Eight-time Olympic medallist on skates, three years retired, running his first marathon for charity. Short-track legs are not marathon legs and he found out over the last 10 km.

title: Marathon
note: Started with the elite-adjacent crowd, finished in the dark after an ankle gave out and a media scrum followed her the length of the Embankment. Walked most of the second half and finished anyway.

title: Marathon (contested)
note: Reported at 3:34, 4:17 and 4:28 depending on the outlet and the race. The ledger keeps her off the table for exactly that reason; she sits here in the contested drawer until a chip time surfaces.

title: Marathon
note: Ran New York, then London, then Lisbon, each one funding Every Mother Counts. The finish times circulate loosely; the fundraising totals do not.

title: 27 marathons in 27 days
note: One marathon a day across South Africa for Mandela's 27 years in prison, finished with a double on the last day. Seven years older than the first attempt and doing it in African summer.

title: 31 marathons and 31 shows in 31 days
note: Lockdown edition: a marathon on a treadmill every day of January, then a stand-up set every evening, in French and German on alternate nights. The set list was arguably the harder half.

title: 7 marathons in 7 days
note: Ran for his old teammate Rob Burrow after a motor-neurone-disease diagnosis, targeted £77,000 and raised over £2.7 million. Rugby league pro, so the engine came pre-built; the week did not.

title: 101 miles in 24 hours
note: Leicester to Leeds, overnight, on roads, in November. Finished on the pitch at Headingley with about ten minutes of the 24 hours left.

title: 401 marathons in 401 days
note: Quit the corporate job, sold the house, and ran a marathon a day for thirteen months across 309 UK locations after years of being bullied. Ran on a stress-fractured back for the last two months.

title: Ran across America five times
note: A Liverpool vet who watched Forrest Gump and took it literally: 15,600 miles of America in beard and running shoes, 422 days on the road, funding two charities.

title: 50 marathons, 50 states, 50 days
note: Finished the run of 50 with the New York City Marathon in 3:00:30, then ran home to California. Career endurance athlete and bestselling author; filed here for scale, not as a peer.

title: Marathon des Sables, 12th overall
note: 156 miles across the Sahara carrying his own food, finishing 12th in a field of a thousand. Double Olympic rowing gold, so the asterisk applies, but nobody rows their way to a desert placing like that.
logistics: MdS entry ~€4,000 plus qualification and medical certificate

title: Rowed the Atlantic
note: 49 days and 19 hours in a small boat with Ben Fogle, two hours on and two hours off, the whole way from La Gomera to Antigua. Second place, and the friendship survived.

title: Oldest Boat Race winner
note: Went back to university at 46, made the Blue Boat, and won — the oldest competitor in the race's 190-year history, four years after a cycling accident left him with a brain injury.

title: Five triathlons in five days
note: Radio 1 breakfast host doing a triathlon in a different British city every day, then presenting the show. Ended up in hospital on a drip before the last one and started it anyway.

title: 116 miles in four days
note: Walked and ran Leicester to Bolton on radio-show hours, live on air the whole way, with feet that made the medical team wince by day three.

title: 350 miles by bike in five days
note: Blackpool to Brighton through February weather, riding for mental-health charities after losing her partner to suicide. Around 70 miles a day on borrowed fitness.

title: Pulled a rickshaw 500 miles
note: Edinburgh to London in nine days dragging a rickshaw, which is cycling with the gearing of a bad dream. The format ran for another decade after him.

title: 24-hour danceathon
note: Twenty-four hours of continuous dancing on live television, which burns roughly what a marathon burns while denying you the dignity of a finish line.

title: 24-hour workout
note: A day and a night of continuous exercise streamed live, on the back of having done PE for a locked-down nation every morning for months.

title: Lived with a Navy SEAL for a month
note: Hired David Goggins to move in and program every waking hour, starting with 100 pull-ups on day one. Also ran a leg of a 100-mile relay solo, which is how the two met.

title: Swam the length of Britain
event: Land's End to John o' Groats · 2013
note: 900 miles up the coast of Britain over 135 days, growing the beard that kept his neck from being flayed by the wetsuit. First person to do it.
logistics: Support boat and crew for four months

title: Swam around Great Britain
note: 157 days without once setting foot on land: six hours swimming, six hours off, around the clock, while his tongue disintegrated from salt water. 1,780 miles.
logistics: Support vessel and crew for five months

title: Climbed a rope the height of Everest
note: 8,848 metres of rope in 19 hours 22 minutes, which is a pull-up session measured in vertical kilometres. He also once ran a marathon dragging a car.

title: Round the world by bike in 78 days
note: 18,000 miles at 240 miles a day, sixteen hours in the saddle, for two and a half months. Beat the existing record by 44 days.

title: Channel swim leg, hypothermic
note: The Windermere leg of her seven-day challenge ended with her being pulled out shaking and vomiting from cold, then getting on the bike the next morning.

title: Cuba to Florida, no shark cage
note: 110 miles in 52 hours 54 minutes on the fifth attempt across 35 years, wearing a silicone mask against box jellyfish. Started the project at 28 and finished it at 64.
logistics: Support flotilla, jellyfish protocol, medical team

title: 1 km swim at the North Pole
note: Eighteen minutes and fifty seconds in water at −1.7°C wearing trunks, to make a point about sea ice. Took him four months to recover feeling in his hands.

title: Swam the length of the English Channel
note: Land's End to Dover the long way — 350 miles over 49 days in trunks and a cap, in a shipping lane, for ocean protection.

title: Swam the Thames, 140 miles
note: Eight days from Lechlade to Westminster through water that gave him giardia, which he named 'Thames tummy' on live television. Raised over £1 million.

title: First woman to swim the Channel
note: 14 hours 34 minutes, roughly two hours faster than any of the five men who had done it before her, in a storm, in a two-piece suit she designed. Two million people turned out for the ticker tape.

title: First Channel swim
note: 21 hours 45 minutes of breaststroke on brandy and beef tea, greased with porpoise oil. He became a Victorian celebrity, then died trying to swim the Niagara rapids eight years later.

title: Four-way Channel crossing
note: England to France and back, twice, in 54 hours 10 minutes — a year after finishing treatment for breast cancer. The tide added about twenty miles she had not planned on.

title: Six-minute underwater take
note: Trained with freedivers to hold breath past six minutes so a sequence could be shot in one take rather than cut. Reported at around six and a half minutes at his best.

title: Solo dive to the Mariana Trench
note: 10,908 metres down, alone, folded into a sphere the size of a fridge for seven hours. Third person ever to reach the bottom, first to do it solo.

title: Underwater box escape
note: Built a career on breath-holds under ice and in nailed crates, and trained in a bathtub to extend them. The figures come from playbills, so read them as theatre with real physiology underneath.

title: Over Niagara Falls in a barrel
note: A widowed schoolteacher who went over Horseshoe Falls in a custom barrel on her 63rd birthday and climbed out concussed but alive. First person to survive it; died penniless anyway.

title: Tightroped Niagara Gorge
note: 1,100 feet of rope, 160 feet above the water, crossed repeatedly — blindfolded, in a sack, on stilts, and once carrying his manager on his back.

title: Everest summit at 65
note: Third attempt, six years after the double bypass and the 7·7·7, and after summiting the Eiger north face at 63. Oldest Briton to the top at the time.

title: Unsupported crossing of Antarctica
note: 2,170 km on foot hauling sledges for 93 days, burning around 10,000 calories a day and losing a quarter of body mass. He later sawed off his own frostbitten fingertips in a garden shed.

title: Walked to the magnetic North Pole
note: On foot, at 63, after three Everest attempts and a summit of Aconcagua. Also the oldest man to reach the pole on foot at the time, and audibly delighted about it.

title: Kilimanjaro attempt
note: Eighteen Grand Slam singles titles and she still had to be stretchered off at 4,600 m with high-altitude pulmonary oedema. Altitude does not care about your backhand.

title: Paramotored above Everest height
note: Took a powered paraglider to around 29,500 feet over the Himalaya at −60°C on oxygen, having been told the engine would probably not run up there.
logistics: Paramotor rated for altitude, oxygen, and a permit nobody wants to grant

title: Crossed the North Atlantic in an open boat
note: Halifax to Scotland in a rigid inflatable through ice fields and a force-8 gale, five men exposed to the weather the entire way.

title: First ascent of Everest
note: A beekeeper from Auckland and a Sherpa from Khumbu, on 1953 oxygen kit and hobnail-era boots, at a time when nobody knew whether the top was survivable at all.

title: Olympic giant slalom
note: The violinist who had sold 10 million records skied for Thailand and finished 67th of 67, more than 50 seconds off the winner, to a standing ovation. The qualifying races were later contested for years.
logistics: FIS points, a federation willing to name you, and a qualifying season

title: Five Winter Olympics in bobsleigh
note: Head of state and bobsleigh pilot across five Games, best finish 25th. Also carried the flag, which is easier.

title: Six Winter Olympics as a pop singer
note: German-Mexican prince, recording artist and photographer who has been Mexico's entire alpine ski team for four decades, latterly in a mariachi-print race suit.

title: Olympic ski jumping, self-funded
note: A plasterer from Cheltenham who was Britain's entire ski-jumping programme, jumped in six-strong prescription goggles that fogged, and finished last in both events by a distance. The rules changed because of him.
display: 70 m and 90 m · last in both

title: Olympic coxless pair
note: Sixth in the final, three years into the Facebook lawsuit and four years before the bitcoin. Oxford blues on the way through.

title: US Open Taekwondo champion
note: Massachusetts full-contact state champion four years running and a US Open lightweight title before he ever picked up a microphone. Retired at 21 from headaches, then took up BJJ and got black belts under two lineages.

title: BJJ black belt under Rorion Gracie
note: Twenty-two years on the mat before the belt, awarded at 61. Al Bundy trained longer for that than most people train for anything.
logistics: About a decade of mat time, minimum

title: BJJ black belt under Renzo Gracie
note: Trained through two decades and a fair amount of tabloid weather to a legitimate black belt. Rank, not race, so the original ledger left him in the footnotes.

title: BJJ brown belt, competed at Pan Ams
note: Trained under Ricardo Miller for years and entered the IBJJF Pan Ams as a competitor rather than a guest. Promoted to black belt posthumously.

title: BJJ brown belt
note: Trains seriously enough to have earned rank from a Machado, and separately ran New York in 3:54. Two different sports, same tolerance for being uncomfortable.

title: BJJ blue belt
note: Trained daily through a period when the alternative was worse, and earned the blue belt in the middle of an album cycle.

title: Went eight rounds with Floyd Mayweather
note: An exhibition with no judges, but eight rounds against the best defensive boxer of the era is eight rounds. He was 34 pounds heavier and still could not land clean.

title: Professional boxing career
note: Turned a YouTube channel into a licensed pro record against a deliberately curated bracket of ex-champions, MMA fighters and one 58-year-old Mike Tyson. The record is real even where the matchmaking is a debate.
logistics: Pro licence, medicals, and a promoter

title: Crossover boxing career
note: Two amateur white-collar fights against another YouTuber turned into a professional card business. Whatever the sport thinks of it, the training camps are real ones.

title: Sub-40 weighted Murph
note: One mile, 100 pull-ups, 200 press-ups, 300 squats, one mile, in a 20 lb vest, under 40 minutes. Self-timed and self-posted, so take the seconds on trust.

title: Gym numbers for Captain Marvel
note: Nine months of programmed lifting up to a 400 lb hip thrust and pushing a Jeep down a road on film. The press numbers vary; the Jeep does not.

title: Boxed himself blind in one eye
note: Sparred with a young artillery officer who landed a blow that detached his left retina. He kept it quiet for years and switched to jiu-jitsu.

title: The two-finger press-up
note: Demonstrated at the Long Beach International Karate Championships and repeated in a hundred retellings since. The training log is real; the numbers attached to it have grown for sixty years.

title: Second overall at Le Mans
note: Fifty-four years old, driving a Porsche 935 for 24 hours in the rain, finishing second overall. He kept racing competitively into his 80s and won a class at Daytona at 70.
logistics: A drive, a licence, and a team

title: Second at Sebring with a broken foot
note: Drove twelve hours in a cast, two weeks after a motorcycle crash, and lost overall by 22 seconds to Mario Andretti. He had also ridden for the US team at the 1964 ISDT.

title: Second in class at Le Mans
note: Ran a real 24-hour campaign in GTE-Am, not a celebrity cameo, and podiumed. Also puts on a cycling event that has raised tens of millions for cancer care.

title: Raced the 24 Hours of Le Mans
note: Four years of club racing and endurance rounds to get a licence and a seat, documented the whole way, then finished the race.

title: Open-wheel and NASCAR racing career
note: Left acting for Champ Car Atlantic at 20, broke his back and hand in testing, and came back two decades later to run a full NASCAR Truck season.

title: Serious road cyclist
note: Owned dozens of bikes, rode with pro teams at the Tour, and used riding to stay sober. No race results, but the mileage was not for show.

title: Five Olympic golds, then Tarzan
note: Never lost a race in ten years, held 67 world records, then spent two decades as the definitive Tarzan. The reverse of every other row in the ledger.

title: Broke his neck and finished the take
note: A water tower slammed him onto a rail track; he got up, finished the day, and only learned years later from an X-ray that it had fractured a vertebra. Did every stunt in every film.

title: Played competitive polo to 52
note: Carried a dislocated shoulder from a gangway accident in 1895 and strapped it to his body to keep playing for another thirty years.

title: Boxed, fished and bullfought professionally enough to write it
note: Sparred in Paris gyms, once refereed a bout between two contenders in Key West, and landed marlin over 400 lb by hand-cranked reel. Also survived two plane crashes in two days.

title: Goalkeeper, Racing Universitaire d'Alger
note: Junior team keeper until tuberculosis ended it at 17. 'All I know most surely about morality and obligations, I owe to football.'

title: Goalkeeper, Trinity College Cambridge
note: Kept goal for Trinity while writing verse between saves, and wrote about the position as the loneliest and most romantic on the field. Took a ball to the head badly enough to be carried off.

title: Goalkeeper, skier, kayaker — later Pope
note: Kept goal as a schoolboy, skied and kayaked as a bishop, and had a pool installed at Castel Gandolfo on the grounds that it was cheaper than another conclave.

title: Goalkeeper, Real Madrid youth
note: On Real Madrid's books until a car crash left him unable to walk for over a year. Learned guitar in rehabilitation, which worked out.

title: Football apprentice, Brentford FC
note: Trained with Brentford's third team as a teenager before deciding the hours were bad and the music was better. Still plays and still has the touch, by his own account.

title: Sub-4:29:20 marathon
note: The single most cited benchmark in the genre. Beat it and you have beaten the reference point for the entire celebrity marathon table.

title: Sub-4:00 marathon
note: Roughly the median finish at a big-city marathon and the first line that means something. Clears Chelsea Clinton, Sarah Palin and Pippa Middleton.

title: Sub-3:30 marathon
note: Gordon Ramsay missed it by 37 seconds in 2004 and has been annoyed about it ever since. About 4:58/km for 42 km.

title: Sub-3:00 marathon
note: The amateur's honours degree, 4:15/km all the way. Matt James missed it by 21 seconds; Harry Styles cleared it by 47.

title: Kelvin Kiptum, Chicago 2023
note: 2:00:35, at 2:51/km, on a course record that redefined what the distance was for. Included as the ceiling of the species, not as a target.

title: Ruth Chepngetich, Chicago 2024
note: 2:09:56, the first woman under 2:10. Same purpose as the men's line: a scale marker at the top of the page.

title: 8,848 m of climbing in one ride
note: Pick a hill, ride it until you have climbed the height of Everest, no sleep. Directly checkable from a single Strava file, which is why the format exists.

title: 500 km between 24 and 31 December
note: Eight days, 500 km, in the worst weather of the year and the fullest week of the social calendar. The purest rolling-window feat there is.

title: 100 miles in one ride
note: The entry ticket to long-form cycling and the first ride where fuelling decides the outcome more than fitness does.

title: 1,000 km in a calendar month
note: Around 33 km a day, every day. Sits between the Izzard tier and ordinary heavy training, and is the cleanest test of whether a body tolerates volume.

title: 89 km, 12-hour cutoff
note: The world's largest ultramarathon and the most humane hard thing in running: twelve hours, a gun at the finish, and the door shut on whoever is still on the road.

title: Full-distance triathlon, 17 hours
note: 3.86 km swim, 180.2 km bike, 42.2 km run, midnight cutoff. Ramsay did it in 14:04 and Sean Astin in 15:30, both inside the door.

title: Ratified solo crossing
note: About 34 km of shipping lane in 15-17°C water, no wetsuit permitted, one crossing per pilot slot. Walliams did it in 10:34; the standard is finishing at all.
logistics: Pilot boat ~£3-4k, two-year waitlist, 6-hour qualifying swim at 16°C

title: Marathon of Hope
note: 5,373 km in 143 days — a marathon a day, every day, on one leg, at 21, until the cancer returned. No table holds this row. It sits apart, where it belongs.
